newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark still vulnerable to EMU doubts.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark still vulnerable to EMU doubts.

text.p: Dollar/mark is likely to come under additional pressure and breach support at 1.7025 as the mark should further benefit from lingering doubts about the European Monetary Union, analysts said on Monday.
Dollar/mark closed at 1.7065/75 versus 1.7125 at the open and after setting a 39-month high at 1.7423 on Friday.
Traders said the mark regained its role as a European safe-haven currency amid concern the euro may not be launched on time on January 1, 1999.
"The dollar is going to go lower," said technical analyst Ture Johnson at Bank of America.
"We have lost nearly four pfennigs since Friday," noted Johnson who described the pullback to a session low of 1.7027 on Monday as quite bearish.
Chartists said the loss of 1.7025-mark support would point to a slide to the 1.6940/60-mark area, and then to 1.6890.
But Johnson expected the yen to cap the mark's advance, noting "Mark/yen peaked in August 1992 and sold off for a full year until August 1993. We may be seeing a similar move."
Mark/yen set a recent high of 69.13 on May 27 and has been losing ground since, retreating below the 66.00 level on Monday before bouncing back to close at 66.15.
Chartists said the mark/yen bounce on Monday may point to a fresh attack on 66.35 resistance -- a run-up likely to invite more sellling.
Johnson said the yen's renewed stamina may also force dollar/yen to grind lower to "111.60 in two or three days."

Bruce English, vice president at ABN/AMRO, predicted "we're in for several more months of amusement and volatility as people one week decide the EMU is an absolutely sure thing or is dead the next one."
"The market is divided between concern the EMU will be weaker or non-existent," English added.

English said dollar/mark should find that "1.6850 is a very strong support level," but that it is difficult to predict whether it will be tested on the near term "because the market is very headline-driven."
"The dollar may well bounce around between 1.73 and 1.6850 marks during a long, hot summer," English concluded.

Chartists said dollar/yen should range-trade near-term between 114.50 and 111.80. As for dollar/Swiss, which gave bearish divergence signals from dollar/mark on Friday, it is gropping for a breakout between strong support at 1.4260 and a big resistance at 1.4475.
